The main takeaway from our work is that

the Cochrane authors often make judgments about random sequence generation that do not follow the Cochrane guidelines, and that the most common mistake is to judge the RoB for this domain as low when the method was not described or was inappropriate.

when assessing the RoB of randomisation, authors should consider the following aspects: (1) whether randomisation method was described, (2) if randomisation method was not described, the authors should assume that the risk of bias for this domain is high, (3) if randomisation was described, the judgment should be low or unclear, (4) if randomisation is not described, the judgment for the random sequence generation should be high and (5) the authors should provide a detailed explanation

authors should not make RoB judgments for randomisation based on a single sentence about randomisation, but they should carefully read the full text of included trials and provide adequate justifications for their judgments.
